extracted.intended_audience: DoD personnel, military planners, intelligence and security professionals, and researchers seeking authoritative doctrine and policy references
extracted.subtask_description: An index-style reference listing DoD and Joint doctrine, directives, instructions, manuals, and other issuance types for intelligence and security; useful for locating authoritative publications and understanding their roles and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: "Doctrine is the fundamental principles by which the military forces or elements thereof guide their actions in support of national objectives. It is authoritative but requires judgment in application." (Joint Pub 1-02)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine establishes guiding principles for action; although authoritative, it is not a set of inflexible rules — practitioners must exercise judgment when applying doctrine to specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint publication hierarchy / framework
rubrics_metrics.description: "The joint publication hierarchy provides a framework for joint doctrine and joint tactics, techniques, and procedures. The organizational structure follows traditional joint staff lines of responsibility to the maximum degree possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the joint publication series and its keystone manuals as the organizing structure for understanding joint doctrine; consult the appropriate series/keystone manual first to identify relevant doctrine and JTTPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keystone manuals as doctrinal foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each series provides for a keystone manual as the first publication in the series. The keystone manuals constitute the doctrinal foundation of the series."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When researching doctrine in a given subject area, start with the keystone manual for that series because it provides the foundational principles and organization for subsequent publications in the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and characteristics of DoD Directives
rubrics_metrics.description: "DoD Directives are broad DoD policy documents containing what is required by legislation, the President, or the Secretary of Defense to initiate, govern, or regulate actions or conduct by the DoD Components within their specific areas of responsibilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directives establish or describe policy, programs, and organizations; define missions; provide authority; and assign responsibilities. They convey high-level requirements and policy that subordinate issuances implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and characteristics of DoD Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: "DoD Instructions implement the policy, or prescribes the manner or a specific plan or action for carrying out the policy, operating a program or activity, and assigning responsibilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions provide the implementing detail for Directives — they prescribe procedures, specific plans, and assignment of responsibilities to execute policy. Use Instructions to find actionable steps and implementation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and subject-group classification of directives/instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The DoD Directives and Instructions are numbered according to the following eight major subject groups: 1000 - Manpower and Personnel ... 8000 - Information Management."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numeric subject-group scheme (1000–8000) to locate and categorize DoD Directives and Instructions by topic area; this classification aids navigation and retrieval of relevant issuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of issuance types and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists many issuance types (Joint Publications, DoD Directives (DODD), DoD Instructions (DODI), DoD Manuals, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Instructions, Directive-Type Memoranda (DTM), Administrative Instructions, Joint Doctrine Notes, etc.) and specific examples for intelligence, operations, security, and related topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that different issuance types have different authorities, scopes, and uses: Joint Pubs provide joint doctrine; Directives articulate high-level policy; Instructions and Manuals provide implementation details; DTMs and memos can provide interim or time-limited policy. Consult the appropriate issuance type for the level of guidance needed and check effective/incorporation/change dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical note: consult online sources and check currency
rubrics_metrics.description: The text notes there are a number of online sources for joint doctrine and related publications and provides many items with effective dates and 'incorporating change' notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using doctrine and policy references, verify the currentness (effective dates, incorporating changes, cancellations) via official online sources; many entries include dates and change histories indicating that currency matters for authoritative use.
